blocks.x: CSM 177 · Computer Appreciation

Microsoft PowerPoint turns raw ideas into professional, presentable slideshows — for sales reports, class presentations, or personal projects. This module covers building, formatting and organising a presentation from a blank slide to a finished slide show.
3PowerPoint views — Normal, Slide Sorter, Slide Show 6common file formats — .pptx, .pptm, .ppt, .pdf, .pps/.ppsx, .wmv 4text alignment options — Left, Center, Right, Justify
By the end of this module, you will be able to…

items: 1Start PowerPoint and create presentations using either a Blank Presentation or a template from Backstage View, and understand slide placeholders and layouts.
2Manage slides and views — insert, copy, delete and move slides, change slide layouts, and switch between Normal, Slide Sorter and Slide Show views.
3Save presentations in the correct format, choosing among .pptx, .pptm, .ppt, .pdf, .pps/.ppsx and .wmv depending on purpose.
4Format text and apply themes — font size/style/colour, bold/italic/underline, alignment, and predefined theme colour/font/effect combinations, including custom background styles.
5Work with text boxes and lists — insert and manipulate text boxes, and customise bulleted and numbered lists (including picture and symbol bullets).
6Insert and edit tables — add tables via placeholder or Ribbon, navigate cells, and insert/delete rows and columns.

blocks.x: Key definitions

Placeholder A dotted-border container on a slide reserved for a specific kind of content — text, a picture, a chart, SmartArt, a table or a video. Placeholders show faint placeholder text and small content icons until you click into them and add content.

Slide layout The arrangement of placeholders on a slide — for example, "Title Slide" or "Title and Content." Each layout has a descriptive name and is chosen from Home > New Slide, or changed later via Home > Layout.
Theme A predefined combination of colours, fonts and effects applied to an entire presentation. PowerPoint's default is the Office Theme; other themes are applied from the Design tab.
Backstage View The screen shown when you click File — used to create new presentations (Blank Presentation or a template), open, save, print and share files.
New Slide→ Choose Layout→ Add Text→ Apply Theme→ Slide Show
Getting started
How to launch PowerPoint, build your first slides, manage them, and move between PowerPoint's three ways of viewing a presentation.
Starting PowerPoint
Starting PowerPoint Click the Start button, type "PowerPoint" into the search box, and click the PowerPoint icon in the results to launch the application.
Creating a new presentation
When PowerPoint opens (or via File > New), Backstage View offers two starting points:

items: ABlank Presentation — starts with no colour scheme or design elements, applying the default Office Theme. Best when you want full creative control.
BTemplate — a pre-designed presentation with a chosen colour scheme and layout. Choose a template, optionally pick a colour variant, then click Create.

blocks.x: Default first slide Every new presentation opens with one slide using the Title Slide layout — a placeholder for the presentation title and a placeholder for a subtitle.
Placeholders & layouts

A placeholder is a box with a dotted border that holds placeholder text (e.g. "Click to add title") and small icons for inserting a Picture, Chart or SmartArt Graphic directly into that placeholder. The overall arrangement of placeholders on a slide is called its layout — for example, "Title and Content" places a title placeholder above a single content placeholder. Every layout has a descriptive name shown when you choose one.
Inserting text into a placeholder

items: 1Click inside the placeholder — the placeholder text disappears and a text cursor appears.
2Type your text.
3Click outside the placeholder (anywhere on the slide) to finish and deselect it.

blocks.x: Inserting & changing layouts

items: +Insert a new slide: Home tab > New Slide group > click New Slide (or the drop-down arrow to choose a specific layout before inserting).
↻Change an existing slide's layout: select the slide, then Home tab > Slides group > Layout, and choose a different layout — existing content is rearranged to fit the new placeholder positions.

blocks.x: Copy, delete & move slides

c: Select slide in the Slides tab → Ctrl+C, click where it should go → Ctrl+V
Select the slide → press Delete, or Home tab > Slides group > Delete
Click and drag the slide thumbnail to a new position in the Slides tab

blocks.x: Normal, Slide Sorter & Slide Show

Normal View The default editing view — shows the Slides tab on the left, the current slide large in the centre, and (often) a notes pane below. Used for adding and formatting content on individual slides.
Slide Sorter View Displays thumbnails of every slide in a grid, making it easy to reorder slides by dragging them, or to get an overview of the whole presentation's flow.
Slide Show View Plays the presentation full-screen, one slide at a time, exactly as an audience would see it — used for rehearsing or delivering the presentation.
All three views are accessed from the View tab, or from the small view-switcher icons at the bottom-right of the PowerPoint window.
Keeping your work
Save As versus Save, and choosing the right file type for how the presentation will be opened, shared or delivered.
Save As vs. Save

items: 1Save As — used the first time you save a presentation (or to save a copy). You choose the location, file type and filename. Accessed via File > Save As.
2Save — used for every save after the first. It updates the same file in place, with no dialog box. Accessed via File > Save, the Quick Access Toolbar, or Ctrl+S.

blocks.x: Common PowerPoint file formats

c: The default file format for PowerPoint 2013/2016 presentations
A presentation that contains macros to run automatically
Saved format that is compatible with older versions of PowerPoint (97 through 2003)
Presentation is saved as a PDF document rather than an editable PowerPoint file
Opens directly in Slide Show view, rather than in Normal (editing) view

blocks.x: Choosing a format Use .pptx for ongoing editing, .pps/.ppsx when you want a double-click to launch the full-screen show immediately, .pdf for a fixed, non-editable copy to distribute, and .wmv when you need a shareable video version.
Look and feel
Entering and formatting text, aligning it within placeholders, and applying (or customising) a theme and background style across the whole deck.
Entering, deleting & selecting text

items: 1Inserting text — click inside a placeholder or text box and type.
2Deleting text — use Backspace to delete text to the left of the cursor, or Delete to remove text to the right.
3Selecting text — click and drag across the text you want to select; a floating hover toolbar with quick formatting commands (Bold, Italic, font, etc.) appears near the selection.

blocks.x: Text formatting commands

c: Changes text size, with live preview as you hover over each size
Changes the typeface used for selected text
Changes text colour; includes a More Colors option for custom colours
Applies bold, italic or underline emphasis to selected text
Nudges text size up or down without opening the size drop-down
Draws a line through the selected text
Adds a drop shadow behind the selected text
Switches selected text between UPPERCASE, lowercase, Sentence case, etc.
Removes all formatting from selected text, returning it to the default style

blocks.x: Aligning text within a placeholder

Align Left / Center / Align Right / Justify These four alignment commands position text within its own placeholder or text box — they do not align text relative to other objects on the slide. Justify stretches each line (except the last) so it fills the full width of the placeholder.
Applying & modifying themes

A theme is a predefined combination of colours, fonts and effects. The default theme in a new blank presentation is the Office Theme. Themes are applied from the Design tab > Themes group: hovering over a thumbnail shows a live preview on the current slide, and clicking applies it to the entire presentation.

Apply before or after adding text? Applying a theme before adding text lets you use live preview to see exactly how your finished content will look as you choose a theme. Applying it after still works — PowerPoint reflows existing text into the new theme's fonts and colours — but you lose the chance to preview it with your real content in place beforehand.

Modifying a theme Customising a theme's colours, fonts or effects (Design tab > Variants, or Colors/Fonts drop-downs) and saving the result creates a new custom theme that can be reused in other presentations.
Background styles

Background Styles Fill variations built from the current theme's colours. Found under Design tab > Background Styles; because they are theme-based, background styles update automatically whenever the theme is changed. For a fully custom background (a solid colour, gradient, picture or texture not offered in the presets), open Format Background.
Structuring content
Adding free-standing text boxes, moving text with copy/paste or drag-and-drop, and customising bulleted and numbered lists.
Insert, move, resize & rotate

items: +Inserting a text box: Insert tab > Text group > Text Box, then click-and-drag on the slide to draw the box, and type inside it.
↔Moving: click the text box border to select it, then click and drag it to a new position.
⤢Resizing: drag one of the sizing handles (small squares/circles) around the selected box's edges and corners.
↻Rotating: drag the small circular rotation handle above the selected box.

blocks.x: Copy/paste vs. drag-and-drop

c: Duplicates the selected text, leaving the original in place and inserting a copy at the new location
Selects text, then click-drag it directly to a new location — the text is moved, not duplicated

blocks.x: Bulleted & numbered lists

Content placeholders support two list types: bulleted lists (each item marked with a symbol) and numbered lists (each item marked with a sequential number). To add list text, click into the content placeholder, type an item, and press Enter to start a new bullet or numbered line at the same level.
Bullet styles, pictures & symbols

items: 1Alternate bullet styles — Home tab > Bullets drop-down arrow, then choose a different preset bullet character.
2Picture bullet — Bullets drop-down > Bullets and Numbering > Picture button, then select an image to use as the bullet symbol for each item.
3Symbol bullet — Bullets drop-down > Bullets and Numbering > Customize, opens the Symbol dialog; use the Font drop-down (e.g. Wingdings) to browse and pick a symbol character as the bullet.

blocks.x: Numbering styles & start value

items: 1Alternate numbering styles — Home tab > Numbering drop-down arrow, then choose a different numbering format (1,2,3 / A,B,C / i,ii,iii, etc.).
2Setting the starting number — Numbering drop-down > Bullets and Numbering > use the Start at: field to set which number the list begins from.

blocks.x: Removing a list Select the list text and click the Bullets or Numbering command again to toggle it off, removing the bullet symbols or numbers and leaving plain paragraph text.

sections.title: Two ways to insert a table

blocks.x: Organising data
Two ways to add a table to a slide, how to move around inside one, and how to insert or delete rows and columns.
Two ways to insert a table

items: 1Via a content placeholder: click the small Insert Table icon in an empty content placeholder — this opens the Insert Table dialog box, where you type the exact number of columns and rows, then click OK.
2Via the Ribbon: Insert tab > Table command, then drag across the grid that appears to visually choose the number of columns and rows before clicking to insert.

blocks.x: Moving between table cells

Cell navigation Move between cells with the mouse (click the cell you want), the Tab key (moves to the next cell, wrapping to the start of the next row; pressing Tab in the last cell adds a new row), or the arrow keys (move up, down, left or right one cell at a time).
Inserting & deleting rows and columns
With the cursor inside a table, the contextual Table Tools > Layout tab appears on the Ribbon, containing the Rows & Columns group:

c: Adds a new row above the row containing the cursor
Adds a new row below the row containing the cursor
Adds a new column to the left of the column containing the cursor
Adds a new column to the right of the column containing the cursor
Removes the entire row(s) containing the cursor or selection
Removes the entire column(s) containing the cursor or selection

blocks.x: Alternate method Right-click inside a table cell to open a context menu with the same Insert (Above/Below/Left/Right) and Delete (Rows/Columns/Table) commands, without switching to the Layout tab.
